components.name: Soil Moisture (Cap.)
components.subtitle: Corrosion-Free Capacitive Probe
warnings: Do NOT submerge electronics above the white dashed line! Lower ADC value = wetter soil.
components.maxReason: K-Comp has at most 2 external analog pins (A3 and A0 with S1-3 OFF).

studentInfo.whatItDoes: Measures how wet or dry potting soil is without rusting (it uses capacitance instead of bare exposed metal!).
studentInfo.howToConnect: Connect VCC→5V, GND→GND, and AOUT → A3 (or A0 with S1-3 OFF).
tips: Never push the board into water/soil past the white dashed line!
Lower analog numbers mean WETTER soil; higher numbers mean DRY soil.

studentInfo.howToConnect: Connect 5V→5V, GND→GND, and SIG → A3 (or A0 with S1-3 OFF).
ideas: Live heartbeat waveform on Serial Plotter
Simple pulse blinker with Red LED

components.subtitle: Single-Lead Electrocardiogram AFE
warnings: CRITICAL HARDWARE FIX: Power AD8232 strictly from 3.3V — connecting 5V permanently destroys the IC!
SAFETY: When wearing ECG electrodes, run laptop on BATTERY ONLY (unplugged from AC mains) for electrical isolation.

studentInfo.whatItDoes: Measures the tiny electrical signals from your heart (electrocardiogram / ECG) through sticky gel electrodes, just like a hospital heart monitor!
studentInfo.howToConnect: STRICTLY connect 3.3V → K-Comp 3.3V (NEVER 5V!), GND→GND, OUTPUT→A3, and LO+/LO− to two digital pins (e.g. D7/D6) to detect if an electrode falls off.
ideas: Live ECG graph on the Serial Plotter
tips: DANGER: 5V instantly destroys the AD8232 chip — always double-check 3.3V!
SAFETY: Always unplug your laptop from the wall charger (run on BATTERY ONLY) while wearing ECG electrodes!

components.protoNote: Seat in the red Prototyping Area to keep the 3.3V wiring and electrode jack stable.

components.name: IR Receiver 940nm
components.subtitle: 38kHz Infrared Demodulator (NEC)
warnings: Restricted to hardware interrupt pins D2 (INT0) or ~D3 (INT1) for jitter-free 38kHz decoding.
components.maxReason: Uses a hardware interrupt (D2 or ~D3) with a single background ISR decoder.

studentInfo.whatItDoes: Receives invisible 38 kHz infrared pulses from the 21-button remote control so you can control your K-Comp from across the room!
studentInfo.howToConnect: Connect VCC→5V, GND→GND, and OUT strictly to hardware interrupt pin D2 (INT0) or ~D3 (INT1).
tips: Must be wired to D2 or ~D3 — normal digital pins cannot trigger the fast interrupt.
Needs line-of-sight between remote and sensor.

components.name: IR Transmitter 940nm
components.subtitle: 38kHz Infrared Emitter LED
warnings: IRremote defaults to Timer2 PWM on pin ~D3 (selectable to any PWM pin in IRremote v4+).
components.maxReason: Uses hardware Timer2 carrier generation with a single transmitter instance.

studentInfo.whatItDoes: Sends invisible 38 kHz infrared signals — turn your K-Comp into your own programmable TV, projector, or robot remote control!
studentInfo.howToConnect: Connect VCC→5V, GND→GND, and DAT → a PWM pin (~D3 recommended).
tips: Fun trick: point your smartphone camera at the IR LED while transmitting — many phone cameras can see the invisible purple glow!

studentInfo.whatItDoes: A stainless-steel waterproof temperature probe you can dip directly into water, tea, snow, or soil (-55 °C to +125 °C)!
studentInfo.howToConnect: Your lab probe already comes pre-equipped with the 4.7 kΩ pull-up resistor built in — no extra breadboard resistor needed! Just connect Red → 5V, Black → GND, and Yellow (DQ) → any free digital pin (e.g. D8).
tips: Pull-up resistor is already built into your lab probe — you do not need to add one yourself!
Only dip the metal tip & black cable in liquid — keep the connector end dry.

components.maxReason: Uses 2 digital pins and a single calibration instance in kcomp_HX711.h.

studentInfo.whatItDoes: Reads tiny voltage changes from metal load cells so you can build your own accurate digital kitchen or bathroom scale!
studentInfo.howToConnect: Connect VCC→5V, GND→GND, DT (Data) → D2, and SCK (Clock) → D8 (or any two free digital pins). Wire the load cells to E+/E−/A+/A−.
tips: Always call tareHX711() with nothing on the scale at startup to zero it out.
Calibrate once using a known weight (like a 500 ml full water bottle ≈ 500 g).

components.protoNote: Use the red Prototyping Area to connect the 4 half-bridge load cells cleanly into a Wheatstone bridge.

studentInfo.whatItDoes: A crisp circular 240×240 full-color IPS screen — ideal for smartwatch faces, speedometers, gauges, and animated robot eyes!
studentInfo.howToConnect: Connect its 4 active I²C pins (VCC, GND, SCL, SDA) to any K-Comp I²C header (H1–H3). Leave the grayed-out DC, CS, and RST pins unconnected.
tips: If using BOTH the onboard OLED and this Round TFT together, switch OLED to Paged mode to save 864 B of SRAM.
I²C address is 0x3D (does not collide with onboard OLED at 0x3C).
